title: Iranian cyber pressure on US and allied infrastructure through the midterms
situation: On 9 November France attributed the October attacks on Danfoss refrigeration controllers at about 700 retail sites to the IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh group (I-1074). Iran-linked intrusions hit US water utilities in at least 12 states from late July and shut a UK power plant for four days. Unit 42 tracks CyberAv3ngers' move to Rockwell controllers and about 60 hacktivist groups, some aimed at Gulf financial sites. Check Point counts Israeli organisations facing about 2,700 attacks a week in early October, up 55% year on year, with Handala tying leaks to the 27 October Israeli election; CTP-ISW reports the DNI warned Iran is in advanced stages of planning attacks on US targets in the region. Defense One, citing two anonymous sources, reports US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers of disrupting freezers at about six military commissaries (I-1028); attribution is unconfirmed.
assessment: Iranian state-linked cyber operations against US and allied critical infrastructure will likely continue through the 3 November midterms. Exposed OT and hacktivist-branded DDoS or data-leak operations are the most probable modes; a disruptive attack on a US payment or banking brand is a realistic possibility.
action: confirm DDoS mitigation headroom for US-facing payment and authentication services and remove internet exposure from any facilities OT
cta: Security operations needs to confirm DDoS mitigation headroom for US-facing payment and authentication services and remove internet exposure from any facilities OT within 7 days.
assumptions: 1) Tehran wants pressure short of provoking US strikes before the midterms; if wrong, expect wipers rather than DDoS. 2) The water-sector intrusions are state-directed; if wrong, targeting is opportunistic and less tied to kinetic events.
alternatives: H2: Iran restrains cyber activity to protect a sanctions-for-transit bargain (US easing is under consideration); the maritime escalation weakens it. H3: activity is mostly exaggerated hacktivist noise; confirmed OT effects in US water systems weaken it.
indicators_of_change: A CISA or FBI advisory naming a new IRGC campaign; claimed attacks on US banks; a US strike on Iranian territory.
what_if: If the US strikes Iran, expect destructive operations against Gulf and US targets within days.

title: Hormuz stays effectively closed to unescorted traffic through the midterms
situation: The IRGC claimed three more tankers struck on 8 November, US strikes reportedly hit Qeshm overnight on 8 and 9 November, and Trump called new strikes quite unlikely while Brent fell to $91.56 (I-1044, I-1046, I-1049). On 9 November Iranian state TV reported projectiles from Sirik toward the strait and explosions on Qeshm (cause unconfirmed), the White House said Task Force Iron Gate operates at full effect, and Araghchi said mediators stopped travelling after the midterms while Rubio said no breakthrough is near (I-1003, I-1004, I-1005). On 5 November Iranian forces claimed at least five tankers hit mines (unverified), UKMTO reported a tanker hit by two projectiles off Qatar, and unnamed Pentagon officials said US forces are poised to resume major operations while Trump has announced no decision. On 4 November the Guards claimed four more tankers destroyed by mines and two vessels halted, and Trump said the US must do 'something large' while the WSJ reports no decision yet. UKMTO counts 30 attacks on commercial vessels in the region in October, a record, and a fatal strike hit an India-flagged vessel off Oman on 3 November; US officials said US forces struck Qeshm on 2 November after the Guards fired on a US aircraft. UKMTO confirmed on 26 October, three days late, that an outbound tanker was disabled by a projectile in the strait on 23 October, and logged a vessel fire 63 nm southeast of Al-Faw on 26 October; JMIC keeps Hormuz at Severe. INTERTANKO counts more than 30 transits a day on the US-escorted route against a pre-war baseline near 138. Iran's strait authority will act against all Sinokor tankers from 1 November, and Tehran has set seven conditions for the US while Qatar mediates a sequenced reopening. Brent settled at $115.81 on 26 October. On 2 November Araghchi said Qatari mediators proposed a two-day sequence for reopening; no agreement exists and Brent traded near $109. UKMTO reported on 3 November that a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles in the engine room 14 nautical miles northeast of Limah off Oman, with no casualties. Brent fell 8.6% to $94.66 on 4 November, from near $118 the previous Friday, as traders priced de-escalation after the midterms; an unnamed senior Iranian official dismissed reports of progress in talks.
assessment: The Strait of Hormuz will very likely remain effectively closed to unescorted commercial transit through at least the post-midterm US decision on a strike package, with UKMTO-reported attacks on shipping at about seven a week region-wide in October while Brent has fallen from near $118 to $94.66 on market expectations of de-escalation, which the physical shipping picture does not yet support. Escorted flows and Saudi rerouting keep some crude moving; a Qatari-sequenced bargain is the main path to reopening.
action: stress-test Gulf-dependent operations, energy-cost and FX exposure, and Gulf staff relocation triggers
cta: Treasury and business continuity needs to stress-test Gulf-dependent operations, energy-cost and FX exposure, and Gulf staff relocation triggers within 7 days.
assumptions: 1) Iran's leadership sees closure as its main leverage before the midterms; if wrong, a quiet bargain could reopen traffic quickly. 2) US escorts cannot restore normal flows; if wrong, flows recover without an agreement.
alternatives: H2: a sequenced bargain (Iran reopens, the US lifts its blockade) reopens the strait within weeks; Iran's seven preconditions weaken it. H3: the US clears the strait by force after the midterms; DNI warnings of Iranian attack planning and US strike preparations keep it live.
indicators_of_change: Agreement on the Qatari five-day sequence; Iran enforcing its Sinokor ban after 1 November; a US strike package on Iran after the 3 November midterms; insurers restoring war-risk cover.
what_if: If a mine or missile sinks a laden VLCC, expect Brent to spike and Gulf states to reroute exports through Red Sea terminals already under Houthi fire.

title: Edge-device exploitation outruns monthly patch cycles
situation: On 9 November CISA added four flaws to KEV including the OpenSSH SSHole bypass, which GreyNoise saw exploited in the wild, and Barracuda and QNAP disclosed further exploitation (I-1068 to I-1071). Previdian saw the first exploitation attempt of OpenSSH CVE-2026-123158 under nine hours after publication, with 20 attempts from 13 IPs by 8 November; no KEV listing is mentioned (I-1029). Lumen links four edge-device zero-days to Volt Typhoon (I-1030). CISA added WordPress Core CVE-2026-119977 to KEV on 3 November. CISA added PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) to KEV on 26 October, five days after PHP's fixes, with a 29 October federal deadline; a researcher logged 35 working shells on honeypots on 24 October, the first confirmed code execution. Siemens (Ruggedcom APE1808 on PAN-OS) and Belden (NetModule, no patch) confirm OT appliance exposure, and CYFIRMA sees a Lazarus-linked operator probing vulnerable hosts in financial institutions. Rapid7 puts the average time from disclosure to exploitation of high-severity flaws at about three days. CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws on 30 October, with Volexity reporting a zero-day chain against fully patched appliances, and Cisco ASA and FTD CVE-2026-76418 on 29 October after Cisco confirmed October exploitation with no workaround. CISA added Apple CVE-2024-27834 to KEV on 4 November.
assessment: Exploitation of newly disclosed flaws in internet-facing edge devices will almost certainly continue to outrun monthly patch cycles. Any internet-facing appliance flaw that reaches KEV, or the pre-KEV early-warning list, should be treated as exploited in the environment until shown otherwise.
action: patch, isolate or take offline any KEV-listed internet-facing device and triage the early-warning list for owned products
cta: Vulnerability management needs to patch, isolate or take offline any KEV-listed internet-facing device and triage the early-warning list for owned products within 72 hours of listing.
assumptions: 1) KEV listing speed tracks exploitation speed; if wrong, the one-day median reflects faster CISA processing, though exploitation evidence is still required for listing. 2) Owned edge inventory is complete; if wrong, unseen appliances carry the risk.
alternatives: H2: the shorter CISA deadlines reflect policy (BOD 26-04) rather than faster exploitation; the publication-to-KEV lag, which policy does not set, weakens it. H3: the 2026 sample is skewed by a few mass-exploitation events; ten vendors in 30 days weakens it.
indicators_of_change: A month with no edge-device KEV additions; vendors shipping fixes before disclosure; CISA lengthening windows.
what_if: If an edge flaw is exploited before a patch exists, isolation and credential rotation are the only controls; pre-stage the runbook.

title: Extortion pressure on financial services keeps rising
situation: Leak-site claims against financial services rose to 150 in the 90 days to 6 September from 68 in the prior 90; Nord Security counts 2,894 ransomware attacks in Q3, led by The Gentlemen (383) and Qilin (363). The FBI attributes 140+ breaches and at least $70M in payments to ShinyHunters' help-desk vishing; Arctic Wolf tracks hundreds of Teams 'IT support' vishing cases ending in Chaos ransomware. A breach of GMO Internet's hosted servers led to unauthorized trades at five Japanese FX brokers, an FSA directive and a refused US$50M ransom demand. An extortion group leaked firewall secrets from a payments vendor serving 11 banks and credit unions on 30 October; the Fed reports no impact.
assessment: Extortion pressure on financial services will likely keep rising through the fourth quarter. For a payments enterprise the most relevant paths are social engineering of the service desk followed by SaaS data theft, and compromise of hosting or platform providers that hold trading or customer credentials, ahead of encryption-led ransomware.
action: require call-back verification for every MFA reset and review third-party OAuth and SaaS token grants
cta: Identity and service-desk owners needs to require call-back verification for every MFA reset and review third-party OAuth and SaaS token grants within 30 days.
csf: PR.AA (Protect: identity management, authentication and access control)
assumptions: 1) Leak-site counts track intrusion trends; if wrong, the rise reflects more aggressive publishing by a few groups. 2) Sector labels are comparable across the publisher's July taxonomy change; labels were mapped back to the earlier scheme to protect this.
alternatives: H2: the rise is an artifact of collection and labeling (survivorship and availability bias, the July taxonomy change). H3: law-enforcement pressure (KillSec, ShinyHunters arrests) cuts activity in the next quarter.
indicators_of_change: A fall in financial-sector claims in the next snapshot; FBI or Europol actions against Qilin or The Gentlemen; vishing campaigns against payment-industry help desks.
what_if: If a payments processor appears on a leak site, expect copycat vishing against its peers within weeks.

title: North Korean revenue operations target financial and technology firms
situation: Elliptic's 9 November analysis shows TraderTraitor laundering Binance proceeds through newly minted memecoins (I-1064, I-1065). DOJ says North Korean IT workers reached at least 70 US companies and are recruiting US facilitators; more than 40 Texas laptop farms were raided. Bitget lost an estimated $387.5M in September in a breach its CEO attributes to North Korea. DPRK-linked theft topped $2B in 2025. On 29 October about $6.36 billion was stolen from Binance across ten blockchains; the FBI attributes it to TraderTraitor and TRM Labs and Chainalysis concur. Binance's incident report traces the theft to a campaign running from a malicious Homebrew install in June through fake recruiter interviews in September to a stolen deployment token on 29 October; Pyongyang denied the attribution on 4 November. Elliptic traced the Binance laundering across about 12,000 wallets on 11 blockchains in four days, with about 44% frozen or seized (I-1020); Kim Yo Jong rejected the attribution on 2 November (I-1019).
assessment: North Korea will very likely continue crypto theft and remote IT-worker infiltration against financial and technology firms. Third-country fronts defeat identity checks that assume an applicant is a US person. The Binance theft is the largest DPRK-attributed theft in this dataset and is consistent with the scale the judgment describes.
stakeholder: HR, talent acquisition and vendor management
action: add live identity verification, device geolocation checks and staffing-vendor attestations for remote technical hires
cta: HR, talent acquisition and vendor management needs to add live identity verification, device geolocation checks and staffing-vendor attestations for remote technical hires within 30 days.
csf: GV.SC (Govern: supply chain risk management); PR.AA
assumptions: 1) Fronts recruited abroad pass standard background checks; if wrong, existing checks suffice. 2) Staffing vendors do not verify the person who works; if wrong, vendor attestations already cover the gap.
alternatives: H2: enforcement and public warnings reduce placements; the July 2026 joint warning describes rising sophistication instead.
indicators_of_change: Indictments naming new facilitators; reports of IT workers inside payment firms; theft from a regulated institution.
what_if: If a DPRK worker is found inside, assume code and secrets exfiltration and rotate keys before confronting the worker.

title: Russian sabotage in Europe continues below Article 5
situation: Estonia's interior minister called Russian acts in Europe state terrorism on 9 November, and hoax threats against flights and newsrooms carried no government attribution (I-1060 to I-1062). Lithuania attributes the 18 October attempted arson at a Vilnius Starlink site to Russia, after Starlink arsons in Poland and Bulgaria; German, Estonian and Polish authorities attribute an explosive drone at Leipzig and an arson at Milrem Robotics to Russia. Romanian F-16s downed two jet-powered Geran-family attack drones, the type Russia uses against Ukraine, over Romanian waters on 17 October. Symantec ties intrusions at European defence contractors to APT28. NoName057(16) pays volunteers in crypto for DDoS. Romania's SRI and DIICOT attributed the 14 September fire beside ROMARM's Carfil plant in Brasov to a Russia-coordinated network whose members were allegedly preparing similar attacks in Germany. Polish police detained a Brasov arson suspect on 28 October and two Germans were arrested on 23 October over the Starlink antenna fire near Sofia.
assessment: Russian-directed sabotage against defense-industrial, logistics and space-ground infrastructure in Europe will likely continue below the Article 5 threshold, with pro-Russian DDoS against financial and government sites alongside it.
action: review perimeter, drone-detection and access controls at data-center and logistics sites in Poland, the Baltics and Germany
cta: Corporate security and facilities needs to review perimeter, drone-detection and access controls at data-center and logistics sites in Poland, the Baltics and Germany within 30 days.
csf: PR.AA (Protect: physical access); ID.RA (Identify: risk assessment)
assumptions: 1) Moscow keeps operations deniable to stay under Article 5; if wrong, expect larger attacks on critical infrastructure. 2) Targets stay tied to support for Ukraine; if wrong, financial infrastructure becomes a direct target.
alternatives: H2: incidents are opportunistic crime wrongly attributed to Russia; repeated official attributions across four states weaken it.
indicators_of_change: Attacks on financial or telecom facilities; NATO Article 4 consultations; new public attributions.
what_if: If a sabotage incident hits a shared data-center campus, expect regulators to ask every tenant for physical-security evidence.

title: PRC access to telecom networks persists
situation: The FBI says Salt Typhoon's intrusions are 'still very, very much ongoing' across 80+ countries, entering through basic vulnerabilities and legacy systems. ATT&CK v20 adds 44 technique relationships to Salt Typhoon. The US seized Flax Typhoon's scanning and phishing infrastructure in October.
assessment: Chinese state actors will likely retain access inside telecom carriers through the next quarter, so SMS and voice one-time codes and unencrypted executive calls should be treated as exposed.
action: retire SMS and voice one-time codes for employees and high-risk customers in favour of phishing-resistant factors
cta: Identity engineering needs to retire SMS and voice one-time codes for employees and high-risk customers in favour of phishing-resistant factors within 90 days.
assumptions: 1) Carrier remediation is incomplete; if wrong, exposure falls faster than assumed. 2) Collection includes authentication traffic; if wrong, the risk is confined to call records and lawful-intercept systems.
alternatives: H2: carriers have evicted the actor since February; no public statement supports eviction.
indicators_of_change: Carrier statements on eviction; new advisories naming carriers; detections of SIM-swap or OTP interception tied to state actors.
what_if: If an executive's carrier account is shown compromised, assume call and SMS content exposure back to the intrusion date.

title: PRC coercion stays below armed conflict, with more friction at sea
situation: Taiwan's MND counted 29 PLA sorties on 21 October, 23 across the median line, and an AIS-dark CCG ship entered Pratas restricted waters on 20 October. Chinese vessels at four Philippine-claimed features rose to 31 in the week to 19 October, and the PLA challenged USS Charleston near Sabina Shoal on 20 October.
assessment: PRC military and coast-guard coercion around Taiwan and Philippine-held features will likely stay below armed conflict over the next 30 days, while confrontations at sea keep rising in frequency.
action: confirm alternate routing for staff travel and data traffic that depends on the Luzon and Taiwan Straits
cta: Asia-Pacific operations needs to confirm alternate routing for staff travel and data traffic that depends on the Luzon and Taiwan Straits within 30 days.
assumptions: 1) Beijing prefers coercion it can calibrate; if wrong, a named exercise could become a quarantine. 2) Manila avoids invoking the treaty; if wrong, US forces become directly involved.
alternatives: H2: a fatal incident at Second Thomas Shoal escalates quickly; no fatality so far.
indicators_of_change: A named PLA exercise; CCG boarding of Taiwan-bound shipping; a fatality at sea.
what_if: If the PLA announces inspection zones, expect insurance and routing disruption within 24 hours.

title: Reciprocal energy strikes through winter
situation: Overnight strikes on 8 and 9 November left more than 600,000 without power in Dnipropetrovsk region (I-1057). Overnight into 9 November Ukraine counted 317 Russian drones and Russia said it hit four substations; on 7 and 8 November raids damaged lines from two nuclear plants and left about 600,000 people without power around Dnipro; a Ukrainian drone fire hit the KINEF refinery in Kirishi (I-1009 to I-1012). Talks open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November with no energy pause announced. On 6 November Ukraine's General Staff reported 196 Russian drones downed or jammed with outages in seven regions including Kyiv, and Russia said it intercepted 142 Ukrainian drones as a fire hit the Afipsky refinery. On 3 November Zelenskiy said Russia launched 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles, and DTEK said three of its five thermal plants were knocked offline; Washington announced trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. Hours after the 21 October Witkoff-Putin meeting, Ukraine said Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and 210 drones at Kyiv, hitting energy infrastructure, and Ukrenergo reported outages in six regions on 22 October. Moscow's mayor says about 630 Ukrainian drones headed for the city the same night. The Kremlin agreed only to technical talks after 10 November, and no readout mentions an energy pause. On 2 November Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 193 drones; Ukrainian drones reportedly hit three Russian refineries between 30 October and 1 November. On 4 November Russia launched 310 long-range drones, 272 intercepted per the Air Force, and struck energy sites in six regions, with emergency outages in Kyiv.
assessment: Reciprocal attacks on energy infrastructure will very likely continue through the winter. Destructive cyber operations against Ukrainian energy operators are a realistic possibility, with spillover risk to European suppliers.
action: brief European operations on energy-supply contingencies and confirm backup power at critical sites
cta: Corporate security needs to brief European operations on energy-supply contingencies and confirm backup power at critical sites within 30 days.
assumptions: 1) Neither side accepts a new truce without US guarantees; if wrong, a deal could pause strikes. 2) Cyber operations accompany kinetic energy strikes; no current item confirms this.
alternatives: H2: a renewed US-brokered truce in exchange for Patriot deliveries; Zelensky named this as his minimum.
indicators_of_change: A new energy truce; a destructive cyber incident at a Ukrainian utility; strikes on gas transit.
what_if: If a cyber attack disables a Ukrainian distribution operator, review shared IT and managed-service providers in the region.
